title: Notes from the live class on circuit laws
content:
Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL): At any node, the sum of currents entering equals the sum of currents leaving, i.e., ΣI_in = ΣI_out.
Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL): In any closed loop, the sum of voltage drops equals zero, i.e., ΣU = 0.
Parallel circuit example: R1=10Ω, R2=20Ω in parallel, find the total resistance. Solution: 1/R_total = 1/R1 + 1/R2 = 1/10 + 1/20 = 3/20, so R_total = 20/3 ≈ 6.67Ω. Current divider formula: I1 = I_total × R2/(R1+R2).
